description: LANID gives annual 30 m maps of irrigated cropland, pasture and hay for the conterminous United States from 1997 to 2017, described in an Earth System Science Data paper. Besides the annual irrigation layers it provides maximum irrigated extent, irrigation frequency, change in frequency between the two decades, irrigation trends and about 10,000 visually interpreted ground reference locations for the eastern United States. The authors report overall accuracy above 90 percent in all years and regions and per-pixel transition accuracy of 81 percent. Coverage is the conterminous United States. The maps are a free download from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0, in an Albers equal-area projection. Caveats: the trend layer is at 6 km, not 30 m, and the series ends in 2017. Simulation uses: the extent and change of irrigated land served by irrigation schemes, for irrigation demand, capacity planning and drought adaptation. Related records: GMIE maximum irrigation extent (data-gmie-global-maximum-irrigation-extent) and the FAO global map of irrigation areas (data-fao-global-map-of-irrigation-areas).
